decisions.question: e-9533

source.question: e-9533
source.value:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t) \,\textrm{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$\mathbf{a} = 2\mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{i}.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =2j+t[i-2j] \\  & =t\,i+(2-2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t = 1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x = t, \qquad
	y = 2-2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(1-y)^{2}\,i+x\,j \\  & =(1-(2-2t))^{2}\,i+t\,j \\  & =(2t-1)^{2}\,i+t\,j \\  & =(4{t}^{2}-4t+1)\,i+t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2-2t)j \\  & =i-2j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =((4{t}^{2}-4t+1)\,i+t\,j)\cdot (i-2j) \\  & =(4{t}^{2}-4t+1)\cdot (1)+(t)\cdot (-2) \\  & =4{t}^{2}-6t+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{t}^{2}-6t+1\,dt \\  & =(\frac{4}{3}{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2}+t){|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{4}{3}-3+1)-0 \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-9532

source.question: e-9532
source.value:
We will use the formula

$$
\int\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t) \,\textrm{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the curve. Making $x$ the subject of the equation, we have

$$
y^3 = x-5
\qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad
x = y^3 + 5.
$$

So, we can parametrize the curve using

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =({t}^{3}+5)\,i+t\,j,\,0\le t\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x = t^3+5, \qquad
y = t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i+x\,j \\  & =t\,i+({t}^{3}+5)\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}+5)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)j \\  & =3{t}^{2}\,i+j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(t\,i+({t}^{3}+5)\,j)\cdot (3{t}^{2}\,i+j) \\  & =t\cdot 3{t}^{2}+({t}^{3}+5)\cdot 1 \\  & =3{t}^{3}+{t}^{3}+5 \\  & =4{t}^{3}+5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{t}^{3}+5\,dt \\  & ={[{t}^{4}+5t]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =1+5-0 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-9531

source.question: e-9531
source.value:
The notation $\displaystyle\oint$ is used to remind us that we're dealing with a line integral over a *closed* curve.

We will use the formula

$$
\oint\limits_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \textrm{d}\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{r}(t)) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t) \,\textrm{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize a circle of radius $1$ centered at the origin. It can be parameterized as 

$$
\mathbf{r}(t) = \cos{t}\,\mathbf{i} + \sin{t}\,\mathbf{j},
\qquad 0 \leq t \lt 2\pi.
$$

So, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x = \cos{t}, \qquad
y = \sin{t}.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =y\,i+x\,j=\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =(\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j)\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j) \\  & =-{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =-(1-{cos}^{2}⁡t)+{cos}^{2}⁡t \\  & =2{cos}^{2}⁡t-1 \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡2t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F(r)\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,dt \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2t]}_{0}^{2\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡4\pi -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
